requirements.title: Program Requirement policy
requirements.summary: Students can substitute Engineering Design ( GE 1110 ) and Engineering Problem Solving and Computation ( GE 1111 ) for Cornerstone of Engineering 1 ( GE 1501 ) and Cornerstone of Engineering 2 ( GE 1502 ) . Mathematics/science requirement: General Chemistry for Engineers ( CHEM 1151 ) , Calculus 1 for Science and Engineering ( MATH 1341 ) , and Physics for Engineering 1 ( PHYS 1151 ) require a grade of C– or higher.

notes: Universitywide and NUpath requirements are referenced but not fully expanded.
Placement substitutions, open elective ranges, grade policies and reuse restrictions require individual review.

Engineering, mathematics/science and professional-development categories allocate portions of the same GE/CIVE/EEMB coursework. Those allocations are policy facts, not extra course credits; totals must not be summed from the inventory.
The GE 1110 plus GE 1111 substitution for GE 1501 plus GE 1502 is retained as a conditional footnote, not an automatically equivalent executable pathway.
Engineering requires CIVE GPA 2.000; named math/science courses require C-minus and writing courses C or higher. NUpath gaps and minimum 30 math/science semester hours require individual review.
Semester-hour units are explicit in the catalog. Published degree totals and category allocations are source rules, not calculated inventory sums.
Course categories are editorial. Source-stated outcomes are paraphrased program aims, not measured graduate outcomes.
The local curriculum is represented; the degree remains partial because full universitywide and conditional policy execution has not been established.
